key_insight: MRI radiomic features added meaningful prognostic signal beyond clinical factors for survival risk stratification in lung cancer brain metastases.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this approach could help identify higher-risk patients more accurately and support more personalized follow-up and treatment planning.
method: Retrospective study of 103 patients with lung cancer brain metastases and matched pre-operative MRI/histopathology.
Extracted radiomic features from T1 post-contrast and T2-FLAIR MRI and combined them with clinical variables.
Trained Cox, random survival forest, and DeepSurv models for overall survival, CNS progression, and leptomeningeal progression.
evidence_signal: The combined clinical-imaging DeepSurv model achieved the best overall survival concordance index (0.728), and imaging-only high-risk groups showed immune-microenvironment differences such as lower tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and PD-L1 expression.
watch_item: This was a retrospective single-cohort study, so external validation is needed before the model can be used routinely in practice.
paper_title: MRI Biomarkers for Brain Metastases in Lung Cancer Using Machine Learning
